request.system: You are a fraud analytics feature engineer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Existing provider features are grouped into families below. Propose new provider-level features that describe HOW a provider bills rather than HOW MUCH, because claim volume already explains most of the label. Use only the claim columns and provider bases the schema allows. Never use the label. (Independent run 1.)

claim_aggregates.name: agent_reimb_std_op
claim_aggregates.rationale: Dispersion of outpatient payments reveals unusual billing patterns such as templated amounts or mixed high-cost claims, independent of volume.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_reimb_median_ip
claim_aggregates.rationale: Typical inpatient payment is robust to outliers and contrasts with the mean to show skew.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_reimb_std_ip
claim_aggregates.rationale: Spread of inpatient payments captures inconsistent case mix or upcoding bursts.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_ndiag_std_all
claim_aggregates.rationale: Low variability in diagnosis counts suggests templated coding.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_ndiag_max_all
claim_aggregates.rationale: Extreme diagnosis counts on a claim flag padded coding.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_nproc_share_ip
claim_aggregates.rationale: Share of inpatient claims with procedures differs from existing per-claim averages and may signal procedure inflation.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_los_std_ip
claim_aggregates.rationale: Uniform length of stay across admissions suggests formulaic billing.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_claimdays_std_op
claim_aggregates.rationale: Variation in outpatient claim duration shows whether billing is formulaic.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_deduct_share_op
claim_aggregates.rationale: Share of outpatient claims with a deductible collected may indicate whether patient cost-sharing is being skipped.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_chronic_std_all
claim_aggregates.rationale: Narrow patient chronic burden spread may indicate a selected or recruited patient population.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_dead_share_pos
claim_aggregates.rationale: Claims linked to deceased beneficiaries suggest billing after death or related irregularities.

claim_aggregates.name: agent_age_std_all
claim_aggregates.rationale: Unusually tight or wide age spread may indicate atypical patient sourcing.

ratios.name: agent_bene_per_claim
ratios.rationale: Low patients per claim indicates repeated billing of the same beneficiaries.

ratios.name: agent_op_reimb_share_ratio
ratios.rationale: Share of money from outpatient billing differs from claim-count mix and shows where the dollars concentrate.

ratios.name: agent_ip_per_bene
ratios.rationale: Inpatient admissions per patient capture repeated admission patterns.

ratios.name: agent_op_per_bene
ratios.rationale: Outpatient visits per patient flag churning of the same patients.

ratios.name: agent_operating_per_attending
ratios.rationale: Operating-to-attending physician ratio indicates a physician network structure.

ratios.name: agent_dgc_per_ip
ratios.rationale: Distinct diagnosis groups relative to inpatient claims shows case mix breadth versus templating.

ratios.name: agent_admitdx_per_ip
ratios.rationale: Diversity of admit diagnoses per admission suggests repeated use of the same justification.

ratios.name: agent_states_per_bene
ratios.rationale: Patients spread across many states relative to patient count may flag unusual patient sourcing.
